title: Uniform PRGs from exponential-time hardness
formal: Does \(\mathrm{EXP}\not\subseteq\mathrm{BPSUBEXP}\) imply the following generator statement? There are integers \(C,k,a\ge1\), a constant \(A\ge1\), and a single deterministic generator algorithm which, for every \(m\ge2\), maps \(d(m)=C\lceil\log_2m\rceil^k\) seed bits to \(m\) output bits in time at most \(A(m+2^{d(m)})^a\), and has this security property: for every fixed uniform probabilistic distinguisher \(T\) running in time \(O(m)\), there are infinitely many \(m\) such that \[\left|\Pr[T(G_m(U_{d(m)}))=1]-\Pr[T(U_m)=1]\right|\le \frac1m.\] The generator is independent of \(T\), and the infinitely many successful lengths may depend on \(T\).
why: Hardness against algorithms is a weaker kind of premise than hardness against arbitrary circuits. A generator with only polylogarithmically many seed bits would turn strong uniform hardness into correspondingly fast average-case derandomization. The remaining gap tests how much of the familiar nonuniform hardness-versus-randomness tradeoff survives with uniform assumptions.

importance.reason: This is the high-end uniform hardness-versus-randomness gap: it asks whether strong algorithmic hardness in EXP yields a single short-seed generator against uniform algorithms. It would sharpen a central connection between lower bounds and derandomization without assuming circuit hardness.
importance.basis: Individual recovery of Vadhan Open Problem 8.7, the Trevisan–Vadhan uniform framework, and later primary discussions and partial tradeoffs.

sentences: The hypothesis says that some exponential-time language resists randomized subexponential-time algorithms.
The question asks whether this uniform hardness yields a single generator with only polylogarithmically many seed bits.
Its output must fool each fixed linear-time probabilistic distinguisher on infinitely many output lengths.
The generator may take quasipolynomial time, but it must be uniform and independent of the distinguisher.
Known low-end and more structured high-end results leave this general hardness-to-randomness implication distinct.

definitions: All machines are multitape Turing machines with a fixed finite program and no advice. Time counts every transition, including input and output processing. Randomized machines use independent fair bits and have their time bound on every random tape. For a time function \(t\), \(\mathrm{DTIME}(t(n))\) consists of languages decided on every input of length \(n\) by a deterministic machine in \(O(t(n))\) time, and \(\mathrm{BPTIME}(t(n))\) uses a randomized machine that is correct on each input with probability at least \(2/3\). Define \(\mathrm{EXP}=\bigcup_{j\ge1}\mathrm{DTIME}(2^{n^j})\) and \(\mathrm{BPSUBEXP}=\bigcap_{j\ge1}\mathrm{BPTIME}(2^{n^{1/j}})\). The intersection permits different algorithms for different \(j\), but each must solve the language on all input lengths. Noncontainment means that some language in the union is absent from that intersection. The generator receives \(1^m\) and an independent seed \(s\in\{0,1\}^{d(m)}\), and produces exactly \(m\) bits \(G_m(s)\). Its one finite program, constants and seed-length exponent are common to all \(m\) and all distinguishers. Integer powers of \(\lceil\log_2m\rceil\) are a concrete normalization of polylogarithmic seed length; extra seed bits may be ignored. The displayed generator running time is the meaning of mildly explicit and may exceed the distinguishing time. A distinguisher \(T\) receives only an \(m\)-bit string, returns one bit, and has a constant \(K_T\) with running time at most \(K_Tm\) on every input and random tape. It receives no input-dependent advice, seed, hard-language oracle or additional auxiliary input. Here \(U_j\) is the uniform distribution on \(\{0,1\}^j\); in each displayed probability the seed or uniform input is independent of the distinguisher’s internal fair random bits. The security quantifiers are \(\forall T\,\forall M\ge2\,\exists m\ge M\) satisfying the inequality. They neither require security at all sufficiently large lengths nor a single length at which every possible finite program is fooled.
answer_criterion: Give a complete mathematically correct Lean proof of the stated implication, with a uniform generator and all seed-length, construction-time and distinguishing guarantees under its hypothesis, or a complete Lean proof of its logical negation. A result assuming nonuniform circuit hardness, hardness only for a smaller complexity class, nonuniform advice for the generator, or a different exceptional-length quantifier does not by itself prove this implication. A limitation on a restricted kind of reduction alone is not a refutation of the implication.

context_blocks.text: This is Open Problem 8.7 with its polylogarithmic-seed, mildly explicit and infinitely-often conventions made explicit. The printed phrase about the generator’s “input” being pseudorandom is read as referring to its output distribution, consistently with the surrounding generator definitions. The inverse-linear advantage is a stated conventional security normalization; the seed is not revealed to the distinguisher.

Trevisan and Vadhan define uniform distinguishing success at all sufficiently large lengths, so failure of every such distinguisher means that each fixed program is fooled infinitely often. Their paper also studies a stronger seed-visible convention; this card does not add that stronger requirement to the textbook’s output-only question.

The textbook distinguishes its known low-end uniform tradeoff from the open high-end implication. It records the corresponding stronger-assumption result when EXP is replaced by PSPACE; that replacement is not the hypothesis asked for here.

Chen, Rothblum and Tell obtain stronger uniform tradeoffs for hard functions with additional uniform-circuit depth structure. Their high-end theorem also uses advice for its BPP simulation. These are material differences from a single advice-free generator derived solely from the EXP noncontainment in this card.

Sdroievski’s 2024 dissertation still describes the high-end uniform equivalence as open. This is a later primary discussion of the gap, rather than a claim that every subsequent manuscript has been exhaustively checked.
